newsitem.title: USA: MCI says new outsourcing service cheaper.
newsitem.headline: MCI says new outsourcing service cheaper.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp said on Wednesday that its new network management outsourcing service would be cheaper than existing services which it said costs $6,000-$12,000 per desktop computer connected per year.
"The average customer will probably be charged $2,700 per user per year," Scott Ross, president of newly-renamed MCI Systemhouse, told a newsconference.

This will include all hardware except the existing personal computer, and free software upgrades, 24-hour customer service and network monitoring. The service is aimed at mid-sized businesses with 50-1,000 desktop computers.

MCI said savings on such a scale are made possible by its centralized customer support, and integrated networks it would supply. It expects to be able to have a new customer up and running in 40-60 days from taking the order.
Ross said MCI did not expect its service to lead to job cuts at clients, but would supplement existing staff.

MCI Systemhouse, which was previously called SHL Systemhouse and was bought last November for $1 billion in stock, has increased its own staff to 6,500 from 5,500 in 12 months to cope with the new services.
"We have three to four times as much business in the pipeline as before (MCI bought the company)" Ross said.
MCI will own the network equipment and software installed for clients, which will be supplied by Compaq Computer Corp, Cisco Systems, Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp.
Expansion abroad will start with Mexico, Canada and Britain, where MCI said it has strong existing partnerships.
